title: Forced Marriage
synopsis: Parents pressuring their children to get married is a big thing in China. Today we learn more about this phenomenon.

fullText.simplified:
你妈妈逼你结婚了吗？

    “你有男朋友吗？”“你结婚了吗？”这些看起来非常容易回答的问题，却让中国单身的年轻人非常头疼。如果你要问现在单身的年轻人最怕什么？那大多数的回答一定是：父母逼婚。
    在中国，不管男女，只要是25岁以上还没有结婚的，基本上都有过被父母逼婚的经历。有些甚至20岁开始就被父母逼婚。逼婚的方式，各地方还不太一样。上海的父母喜欢用言语逼婚，见面、打电话，只要一有机会就会和孩子聊结婚；四川的父母喜欢叫上亲戚朋友一起逼孩子结婚；广西的父母喜欢给孩子安排相亲，逼孩子去相亲。有些父母甚至会说：“不结婚就别回家！”
    因为怕被父母逼婚，现在有些年轻人过年就带个假男朋友/假女朋友回家，暂时应付几天。网络上还出现了“租男朋友/女朋友”的服务。
fullText.traditional:
你媽媽逼你結婚了嗎？

    “你有男朋友嗎？”“你結婚了嗎？”這些看起來非常容易回答的問題，卻讓中國單身的年輕人非常頭疼。如果你要問現在單身的年輕人最怕什麼？那大多數的回答一定是：父母逼婚。
    在中國，不管男女，只要是25歲以上還沒有結婚的，基本上都有過被父母逼婚的經歷。有些甚至20歲開始就被父母逼婚。逼婚的方式，各地方還不太一樣。上海的父母喜歡用言語逼婚，見面、打電話，只要一有機會就會和孩子聊結婚；四川的父母喜歡叫上親戚朋友一起逼孩子結婚；廣西的父母喜歡給孩子安排相親，逼孩子去相親。有些父母甚至會說：“不結婚就別回家！”
    因為怕被父母逼婚，現在有些年輕人過年就帶個假男朋友/假女朋友回家，暫時應付幾天。網絡上還出現了“租男朋友/女朋友”的服務。

raw.synopsis: Parents pressuring their children to get married is a big thing in China. Today we learn more about this phenomenon.
sentence_translations: Did your mother force you to marry?
These questions are seemingly very simple to answer, but they are a headache for young Chinese singles.
What if you were to ask today's young singles what they are the most afraid of?
The majority of them would undoubtedly respond: being forced by their parents to marry.
In China, no matter if you're a boy or a girl, basically everyone over 25 and still unmarried has experienced being pressured about marriage by their parents.
Some even begin being pressured to marry when they are 20 years old.
The way of forced marriage is different in different regions.
Parents in Shanghai like to use words to put pressure; whenever they meet or talk on the phone, they take every chance to talk to their child about marriage.
Sichuan parents like to call upon friends and relatives to together put pressure on the children to get married.
Parents in Guangxi like to arrange blind dates for their children, which they force them to attend.
Some parents even go as far as to say: “If you don't get married, don't bother coming home anymore!”
Because they are scared of being forced into marriage by their parents, ..
.. some young people now bring a fake boyfriend or girlfriend with them home to spend New Year's, to temporarily endure those few days.
Online services offering “Boyfriend/girlfriend for rent” have also appeared.
